name: SWE-Gym
description: SWE-Gym is the first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. Tasks are sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories, with pre-configured executable environments and expert-validated test cases. SWE-Gym also includes SWE-Gym Lite (230 instances) for rapid prototyping and SWE-Gym Raw (64,689 instances spanning 358 Python repositories) without executable environments.
creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada. PMLR 267.
rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym was constructed by identifying Python repositories using SEART GitHub search, extracting task instances from pull requests using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script, versioning instances, and manually configuring executable environments with pre-installed dependencies. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours. Instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: SWE-Gym Raw instances do not contain executable environments or a guarantee that unit tests are effective in evaluating the correctness of a solution. Instances that failed environment setup validation were filtered out.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world GitHub issues and pull requests from 11 popular open-source Python repositories (pandas, MONAI, moto, mypy, dvc, dask, modin, pydantic, conan, hydra, bokeh). Repositories were selected using SEART GitHub search, filtering for repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Repositories created before July 1, 2022 were included. The dataset construction and collection process details do not specify an explicit end date beyond the paper's publication.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Instances were versioned by associating them with version numbers and setting up environments version-by-version. Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance using relevant configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation. Pre-built Docker images were created for each instance for full reproducibility, totaling 6 TB.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to convert repositories into task instances. Instances were versioned using a generalized SWE-Bench versioning script. Executable environments were manually configured. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to filter out instances where the gold patch did not pass more unit tests than the original code. SWE-Gym Lite was filtered following the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline, excluding tasks requiring editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Executable environments were manually configured by a subset of the authors using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation. Validation was performed using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than the original code. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were done by a subset of the paper's authors.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEART GitHub search, SWE-Bench instance extraction script, SWE-Bench versioning script, SWE-Bench execution-based validation script, SGLang, torchtune, Unsloth
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-Gym, models, agent trajectories, pre-built Docker images, and training pipeline are publicly released. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries. As agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code. The authors encourage future work to explore frameworks for responsible deployment, including considerations around security, safety, and economic impacts.
rai:dataBiases: Task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with pandas comprising nearly one-third of total tasks and bokeh representing only one percent. Repeated sampling shows that task success probability follows a long-tail distribution biased toward easier tasks. Automatic environment setup scripts (used by concurrent work) bias environments away from tasks with complex dependencies. The authors address this through manual configuration and per-instance capping.
rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories (11), types of tasks, and programming languages (Python only). Tasks in SWE-Gym are on average harder than those in SWE-Bench. The dataset is currently limited to 2,438 instances due to the manual effort required for environment configuration. Performance improvements are currently limited by compute budget for sampling rather than the number of tasks.
rai:dataUseCases: Training language model-based software engineering agents via rejection sampling fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Training verifier (outcome-supervised reward) models for inference-time scaling. Evaluating SWE agent performance. Rapid prototyping using SWE-Gym Lite. Future research in automatic dataset synthesis and SWE agent development.
